ordered_diagnoses: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries

facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s with a history of hypertension
sudden-onset chest pain
no history of any acute febrile illness
no family history of sudden cardiac death
tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min
blood pressure was normal
White blood cell count: 14,300/µL
Serum calcium: within normal limits
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

support_spans: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm
concepts.why: The presence of an adrenal mass and elevated troponin levels suggest a diagnosis of pheochromocytoma, which can cause cardiac damage and elevated white blood cell count.

contradict_spans: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm
concepts.why: The presence of sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin and brain-type natriuretic peptide levels, and apical ballooning on left ventriculography are characteristic of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.

tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min
concepts.why: The patient's history of hypertension and tachycardia could suggest a hypertensive emergency, but the normal blood pressure reading contradicts this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries
concepts.why: The ECG findings of ST-segment elevation in multiple leads with normal coronary arteries on angiography point towards this condition.

rationales.F02: Sudden-onset chest pain is a common symptom of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F05: Tachycardia can be seen in various conditions including pheochromocytoma, Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin levels are indicative of myocardial injury, which can be seen in myocardial infarction and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F10: Elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide levels are often seen in conditions with increased myocardial wall stress, such as heart failure and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F11: The described ECG changes are consistent with myocardial infarction and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F12: The presence of an adrenal mass is highly suggestive of pheochromocytoma, which can cause secondary effects on the heart.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on the contrast-enhanced abdominal CT, which is specific to Pheochromocytoma, decided it.
